summary: TerraLuna(Earth Analog Finder) is an interactive web map that ranks places on Earth by how well they resemble a chosen Moon or Mars site. Pick a target, such as the Shackleton Crater rim or Jezero Crater, and the tool scores 22 Earth sites on slope, roughness, temperature extremes, aridity and volcanic geology using open NASA data. Every score is explainable: users can change factor weights, compare sites side by side, and see for each site where the analogy breaks down. An AI model writes plain-language explanations from the data only. It matters because mission teams need analog sites to test equipment and methods before flying, and many analogs are poorly characterized.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

TerraLuna(Earth Analog Finder) helps mission planners and the public discover which Earth locations best rehearse a Moon or Mars site. Users choose a target (Shackleton Crater rim, Malapert Massif, Jezero Crater or Gale Crater), then see a ranked list and map of 22 Earth candidate sites, including lesser-known ones such as the Danakil Depression, Salar de Uyuni, Dasht-e Lut, Tibesti, Pinacate and Svalbard, not only famous analogs.

HOW IT WORKS

Each site is described by five factors normalized to 0-1: slope, roughness, temperature extremes, aridity and volcanic/basaltic geology. Per-factor similarity is 1 minus the absolute difference; the overall score is a weighted average, so users can re-weight factors with sliders and the ranking updates instantly. Earth values come from NASA POWER climate data and a global elevation dataset. Moon slope and roughness are measured from the LRO LOLA south-polar DEM using the same 5x5 grid method as the Earth sites, so values are comparable. A FastAPI backend serves the data and an AI explanation endpoint; the AI only receives the numbers in our dataset and falls back to a template if unavailable.

WHERE ANALOGIES BREAK DOWN

Each site shows its own limits, and every explanation notes that Earth cannot reproduce reduced gravity, vacuum or thin atmosphere, or radiation. Values that are estimates, not measurements, are labelled "est." in the app.

BENEFITS AND GOALS

A transparent, adjustable way to compare analog candidates, to find overlooked sites, and to explain why a site is or is not a good analog. We hope it becomes a starting point for a global, systematic analog search.

TOOLS

Python, FastAPI, NumPy, rasterio, pyproj, matplotlib; JavaScript, Leaflet, Chart.js; Google Gemini API; hosted on Render. Code: https://github.com/Drish23-sys/Nasa_challenge

LIMITATIONS

Curated set of 22 sites, not a global search. Earth temperature is annual air-temperature range while Moon/Mars use surface temperature (a proxy). Moon temperature ranges, geology tags and Mars slope/roughness are team estimates and are labelled as such.
dataRefs: LRO LOLA south-polar digital elevation model, product LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ (NASA PGDA)
NASA GIBS, Blue Marble imagery, used as the map basemap
